newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei likely to weaken, eyes on 20,000 line.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei likely to weaken, eyes on 20,000 line.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key benchmark is likely to weaken in the Wednesday session as investors stay on the sidelines following a slide on Tuesday brought about partly by the widening Nomura Securities Co Ltd scandal, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the 225-share Nikkei average ended down 429.44 points, or 2.08 percent, at 20,175.52. Its September futures tumbled 470 points to end at 20,100.
"It could go either way today," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities. "If the scandal worries escalate, The Nikkei could be in for brief dip below 20,000."
"But on the other hand, Tokyo stocks in London were a bit firmer and Chicago Nikkei 225 futures ended above the Osaka close, which could mean the downside could be limited," he added.
Brokers added that eyes were on foreign investors who have bought stocks actively in recent sessions, boosting the market and inspiring domestic investors to buy.

"The supply/demand situation had been fairly good recently but after the end-June book closing, buying by foreign investors petered out," one broker said. "How much lower the Nikkei goes depends whether foreigners resume buying or not."
